**Paper:** figure style and variable names  ·  **Source:** [fluxpy/figstyle.py](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/figstyle.py)

the single styling module of all manuscript figures.

All manuscript figure scripts (`figures_manuscript/fig*.py`) take their style
from here only; no figure script sets rcParams, font sizes or colours itself.

**Design contract**

1. **Physical size.**  Figures are built at their printed size (Copernicus/AMT
   two-column layout on DIN A4).  The .tex includes them without scaling
   (`\includegraphics{...}`, no `width=`), so fonts print at exactly the
   size set here.  Widths:

   | constant | cm | Copernicus figure class |
   |---|---|---|
   | COL_W | 8.3 | one column  (the default) |
   | MID_W | 12.0 | 1.5 columns |
   | FULL_W | 17.0 | full text width (two columns) |

2. **One font size.**  [`FONT_SIZE`](#fluxpy.figstyle--constants) is used for all text (labels, ticks,
   legends, annotations) and equals the journal text size.  It is set here for
   the whole manuscript, never per figure.

3. **Exact width.**  [`save()`](#fluxpy.figstyle.save) writes without a tight bounding box, so the
   PDF keeps the exact physical width.  Use `layout="constrained"` (the
   default from [`figure()`](#fluxpy.figstyle.figure)) so nothing overflows.

Typical figure script:

```python
from fluxpy import figstyle as fs
fs.apply()
fig, ax = fs.figure(width=fs.COL_W, aspect=0.8)
ax.plot(x, y, color=fs.C["H_obs_bulk"], label=fs.L["H_obs_bulk"])
fs.panel_label(ax, "(a)")
fs.save(fig, "fig06_flux_scatter")
```

(fluxpy.figstyle--constants)=
## Constants

| Name | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CM` | `1.0 / 2.54` = `0.393701` | one centimetre in inches |
| `COL_W` | `8.3 * CM` = `3.26772` | 3.27 in — single column, the default |
| `MID_W` | `12.0 * CM` = `4.72441` | 4.72 in — 1.5 column |
| `FULL_W` | `17.0 * CM` = `6.69291` | 6.69 in — full text width |
| `MAX_H` | `23.0 * CM` = `9.05512` | keep every figure below this (A4 page minus caption) |
| `FONT_SIZE` | `9.0` | pt, for every text element of every figure |
| `C` | `dict` with the keys `H_obs_ec`, `H_obs_bulk`, `H_rs_bulk`, `H_era_bulk`, `H_era_diag`, `H_car_diag` | colour of each flux estimate (colour-vision-deficiency safe), keyed by variable name |
| `GREY` | `"0.45"` | 1:1 lines, reference lines |
| `GRID` | `"0.82"` | zero lines / faint guides |
| `FLUX_UNIT` | `r"(W m$^{-2}$)"` | unit of a flux axis label |
| `FLUX_AXIS` | `r"$H_\mathrm{S}$ (W m$^{-2}$)"` | generic flux axis label |
| `OUT_DIR` | `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "figures_manuscript" / "output"` | where [`save()`](#fluxpy.figstyle.save) writes the figures: figures_manuscript/output of the repository |
| `RC` | `dict` with 35 entries | matplotlib rcParams set by [`apply()`](#fluxpy.figstyle.apply): fonts, axes, ticks, lines, legend, layout, output |

:::{dropdown} RC (definition)
````python
RC = {
    # fonts — ONE size for everything
    "font.family": "sans-serif",
    "font.sans-serif": ["Arial", "Helvetica", "DejaVu Sans"],
    "font.size": FONT_SIZE,
    "axes.labelsize": FONT_SIZE,
    "axes.titlesize": FONT_SIZE,
    "xtick.labelsize": FONT_SIZE,
    "ytick.labelsize": FONT_SIZE,
    "legend.fontsize": FONT_SIZE,
    "figure.labelsize": FONT_SIZE,
    "mathtext.fontset": "dejavusans",
    "mathtext.default": "regular",

    # house style: open axes, ticks out
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.linewidth": 0.8,
    "xtick.direction": "out",
    "ytick.direction": "out",
    "xtick.major.size": 3.0,
    "ytick.major.size": 3.0,
    "xtick.major.width": 0.8,
    "ytick.major.width": 0.8,
    "xtick.minor.size": 1.8,
    "ytick.minor.size": 1.8,
    "xtick.minor.width": 0.6,
    "ytick.minor.width": 0.6,

    # lines / markers
    "lines.linewidth": 1.2,
    "lines.markersize": 4,

    # legend
    "legend.frameon": False,
    "legend.borderpad": 0.3,
    "legend.labelspacing": 0.35,
    "legend.handlelength": 1.4,

    # layout: constrained by default → figures keep their EXACT physical size
    "figure.constrained_layout.use": True,
    "figure.dpi": 150,
    "savefig.dpi": 300,

    # vector output: embed TrueType fonts
    "pdf.fonttype": 42,
    "ps.fonttype": 42,
}
````

(fluxpy.figstyle.apply)=
### `apply`

```python
apply() -> None
```

Activate the manuscript style (call once, right after the imports).

**Returns** `None`

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/figstyle.py#L132-L134)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/figstyle.py, lines 132–134)
````python
def apply() -> None:
    """Activate the manuscript style (call once, right after the imports)."""
    mpl.rcParams.update(RC)
````

(fluxpy.figstyle.figure)=
### `figure`

```python
figure(width: float = COL_W, aspect: float = 0.75, **kwargs)
```

`plt.subplots` at physical size: `figsize=(width, width*aspect)`.

Any extra kwargs (`nrows`, `ncols`, `sharex` …) pass through.
For a custom GridSpec layout use [`gridfig`](#fluxpy.figstyle.gridfig) instead — this function
already creates axes, and adding a gridspec on top leaves a stray empty
axes underneath that breaks constrained layout.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `width` | `float` | `COL_W` (= `3.26772`) |
| `aspect` | `float` | `0.75` |
| `**kwargs` |  |  |

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/figstyle.py#L137-L145)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/figstyle.py, lines 137–145)
````python
def figure(width: float = COL_W, aspect: float = 0.75, **kwargs):
    """``plt.subplots`` at physical size: ``figsize=(width, width*aspect)``.

    Any extra kwargs (``nrows``, ``ncols``, ``sharex`` …) pass through.
    For a custom GridSpec layout use :func:`gridfig` instead — this function
    already creates axes, and adding a gridspec on top leaves a stray empty
    axes underneath that breaks constrained layout.
    """
    return plt.subplots(figsize=(width, width * aspect), **kwargs)
````
:::

(fluxpy.figstyle.gridfig)=
### `gridfig`

```python
gridfig(width: float = COL_W, aspect: float = 0.75, **kwargs)
```

Figure without axes at physical size, for `fig.add_gridspec` layouts.

Constrained layout is on via the style, so `add_gridspec` +
`add_subplot` compose cleanly:

```python
fig = fs.gridfig(width=fs.COL_W, aspect=1.7)
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 4, height_ratios=[2, 1, 1])
ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
```

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `width` | `float` | `COL_W` (= `3.26772`) |
| `aspect` | `float` | `0.75` |
| `**kwargs` |  |  |

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/figstyle.py#L148-L158)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/figstyle.py, lines 148–158)
````python
def gridfig(width: float = COL_W, aspect: float = 0.75, **kwargs):
    """Figure without axes at physical size, for ``fig.add_gridspec`` layouts.

    Constrained layout is on via the style, so ``add_gridspec`` +
    ``add_subplot`` compose cleanly::

        fig = fs.gridfig(width=fs.COL_W, aspect=1.7)
        gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 4, height_ratios=[2, 1, 1])
        ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
    """
    return plt.figure(figsize=(width, width * aspect), **kwargs)
````
:::

(fluxpy.figstyle.panel_label)=
### `panel_label`

```python
panel_label(ax, label: str, x: float = -0.02, y: float = 1.02) -> None
```

Bold panel letter '(a)' at the top-left corner, outside the axes.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `ax` |  | required |
| `label` | `str` | required |
| `x` | `float` | `-0.02` |
| `y` | `float` | `1.02` |

**Returns** `None`

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/figstyle.py#L161-L164)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/figstyle.py, lines 161–164)
````python
def panel_label(ax, label: str, x: float = -0.02, y: float = 1.02) -> None:
    """Bold panel letter '(a)' at the top-left corner, outside the axes."""
    ax.text(x, y, label, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=FONT_SIZE,
            fontweight="bold", va="bottom", ha="right")
````
:::

(fluxpy.figstyle.save)=
### `save`

```python
save(fig, name: str, png: bool = True) -> Path
```

Save `OUT_DIR/name.pdf` (+ `.png`) at the exact physical size.

`bbox_inches='tight'` is deliberately not used: a tight crop changes the
physical width and rescales the fonts in print.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `fig` |  | required |
| `name` | `str` | required |
| `png` | `bool` | `True` |

**Returns** `Path`

[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/figstyle.py#L167-L180)

:::{dropdown} Source code (fluxpy/figstyle.py, lines 167–180)
````python
def save(fig, name: str, png: bool = True) -> Path:
    """Save ``OUT_DIR/name.pdf`` (+ ``.png``) at the exact physical size.

    ``bbox_inches='tight'`` is deliberately not used: a tight crop changes the
    physical width and rescales the fonts in print.
    """
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    pdf = OUT_DIR / f"{name}.pdf"
    fig.savefig(pdf, metadata={"Creator": "BACSAM-II figures_manuscript"})
    if png:
        fig.savefig(OUT_DIR / f"{name}.png")
    w, h = fig.get_size_inches()
    print(f"{name}: {w / CM:.1f} x {h / CM:.1f} cm  ->  {pdf}")
    return pdf
````
:::
